fresh box: no config · run 'caramelo commander init' to name this machine

An environment is an isolated, disposable copy of an app on the machine:
a git worktree on its own branch, its own block of ports, a container and a
named volume per dependency, and the variables that tie them together. Many
of them can exist at once without sharing anything.

The app is the repository you are standing in; --app (or CARAMELO_APP) names
it explicitly when you are not.

Usage:
  caramelo env [flags]

Examples:
  caramelo env create feat-x --from main
  caramelo env list
  caramelo env show feat-x
  caramelo env destroy feat-x --yes


Flags:
      --app string   application these environments belong to (default: the checkout you are in)
  -h, --help         help for env

Global Flags:
      --fleet string      fleet to talk to, by its name in the commander config (default: the app's fleet, then the default fleet)
      --json              print machine-readable JSON on stdout
      --machine string    raw ssh target to talk to, for a machine that is in no fleet yet: user@host[:port], or 'local'
      --progress string   how progress is written to stderr: text (default) or json, one event per line

10 commands are hidden here; 'caramelo manual --role all' lists every command of every role.
